column1: # Where each woven Portuguese plural in lex-pt.tsv was read.
# A noun row weaves its second form under an English plural, and the tooltip
# prints that form as the word the reader met. On 2026-10-08 every woven
# Portuguese plural was read in the headword line of English Wiktionary's
# Portuguese entry for its noun, rendered as a reader sees it, because the
# raw template mostly leaves the plural to Wiktionary's module:
# {{pt-noun|m}} prints "homem m (plural homens)". 177 of the 178 are among
# the plurals their own noun's line prints. The 178th, chão, floor, was
# woven chões, a form English Wiktionary has no page for, where its line
# prints "chão m (plural chãos)": a noun in -ão takes -ãos, -ães or -ões by
# its history, and chão takes -ãos, as mão is mãos. It weaves chãos since
# quote is the clause of that line which prints the plural, its qualifiers
# kept, or "invariable" where the line says the plural is the singular. A
# page holds every word of one spelling, so the clause is this word's own
# noun's, of the seed's gender and sense. One page holds a second noun of
# this spelling with another plural: cão, dog, is "plural cães" where cão, a
# tests/tools/plurals.test.ts requires every noun lex-pt.tsv weaves in a
# second form to have a line here with that form, citing the noun's own
# entry, its quote printing the form, and fails on a line outliving its row.
